sections.reason: Header, status, copyright and abstract. The abstract states the document replaces RFC 1034 Section 4.3.4 and that negative caching should no longer be seen as optional; the lowercase should is not a BCP 14 keyword in this post-RFC 2119 document, and Section 8 restates it.

Terminology. The RFC 2119 key-words paragraph and the definitions of negative caching, QNAME, NXDOMAIN, NODATA and FORWARDER. The lowercase should about ordering CNAME records states no capitalised obligation.
Negative Responses: introduction to the two kinds, with no normative sentence.
Name Error: defines NXDOMAIN and its four types by authority-section content, against a referral. Descriptive, no keyword.
Special Handling of Name Error: the lowercase recommendation that authoritative servers send only TYPE 2 NXDOMAIN, and the note on forcing the authority flag for forwarders. No capitalised keyword.
No Data: defines NODATA and its three types, and how it is told from a referral. Descriptive, no keyword.

Special Handling of No Data: the lowercase recommendation to send only TYPE 2 NODATA and the lowercase must to query again using the QNAME when a server fails to set NXDOMAIN beside CNAMEs. No capitalised keyword.

Negative Answers from Authoritative Servers. Two capitalised MUSTs, mapped to RFC2308-3-1 and RFC2308-3-2. The SOA TTL rule (minimum of MINIMUM and the SOA's TTL) and the lowercase should on trimming the SIG TTL carry no keyword.

SOA Minimum Field. Deprecates MINIMUM as the minimum TTL of every RR in a zone (the RFC 1035 Section 3.3.13 meaning), adds the $TTL master-file directive, and makes the negative-response TTL MINIMUM's one meaning. No capitalised keyword; the lowercase should on providing a default-TTL mechanism binds a primary server reading master files.

Caching Negative Answers. Three capitalised MUST-level sites, mapped to RFC2308-5-1, RFC2308-5-2 and RFC2308-5-3. The advisory SHOULD NOT on caching a negative response without an SOA carries no site and is RFC2308-5-4. The lowercase shoulds on the NXDOMAIN and NODATA cache keys, on SIG records, and on a negative cache limit carry no keyword.

Negative answers from the cache. Two capitalised MUSTs, mapped to RFC2308-6-1 and RFC2308-6-2. The two advisory SHOULDs carry no site: the SIG record cached with an NXT (RFC2308-6-3) and the implicit referral (RFC2308-6-4).
Other Negative Responses: introduction, no normative sentence.

Server Failure, headed OPTIONAL. The MAY to cache a server failure response carries no site (RFC2308-7.1-3). Site 7.1:1 holds two obligations conditional on that MAY: the MUST NOT on the five-minute limit, mapped to RFC2308-7.1-1, and the MUST on the query tuple, which is its second clause and is listed here as RFC2308-7.1-2.

Dead / Unreachable Server, headed OPTIONAL. The MAY to cache a dead server indication carries no site (RFC2308-7.2-3). Two capitalised MUST-level sites conditional on it, mapped to RFC2308-7.2-1 and RFC2308-7.2-2. The lowercase may on deeming a server dead after 120 seconds carries no keyword.

Changes from RFC 1034. One capitalised MUST, mapped to RFC2308-8-1, and the MAY to cache non-authoritative negative answers (RFC2308-8-2). The lowercase musts restate Sections 5 and 6 and carry no keyword.
History of Negative Caching, which states it forms no part of the technical specification.
Example of a signed zone's initial and cached NXDOMAIN response. Illustrative, no keyword.
Security Considerations: the high-TTL NXDOMAIN denial of service and TTL sanity checking. No capitalised keyword.

sites.quote: Name servers authoritative for a zone MUST include the SOA record of the zone in the authority section of the response when reporting an NXDOMAIN or indicating that no data of the requested type exists.
If the containing zone is signed [RFC2065] the SOA and appropriate NXT and SIG records MUST be added.
This TTL decrements in a similar manner to a normal cached answer and upon reaching zero (0) indicates the cached negative answer MUST NOT be used again.

The NXT record, if it exists in the authority section of a negative answer received, MUST be stored such that it can be be located and returned with SOA record in the authority section, as should any SIG records in the authority section.
The NXT record MUST have the same owner name as the query name for NODATA responses.

When a server, in answering a query, encounters a cached negative response it MUST add the cached SOA record to the authority section of the response with the TTL decremented by the amount of time it was stored in the cache.
If a NXT record was cached along with SOA record it MUST be added to the authority section.
If it does so it MUST NOT cache it for longer than five (5) minutes, and it MUST be cached against the specific query tuple <query name, type, class, server IP address>.
If it does so it MUST NOT be deemed dead for longer than five (5) minutes.

The indication MUST be stored against query tuple <query name, type, class, server IP address> unless there was a transport layer indication that the server does not exist, in which case it applies to all queries to that specific IP address.
The SOA record from the authority section MUST be cached.
